issues.detail: The Hebrew 'הַצְּפִרָה' (hatzefirah) means 'the crown' or 'the diadem' (from צָפִיר, a crown/garland), not '冠冕' (crown) — actually '冠冕' is correct for 'crown'. However, 'הַמַּטֶּה' (hammatteh) means 'the rod/staff/scepter' (a branch or staff), not '杖已飛逝' (the staff has flown away). The Hebrew 'צָץ הַמַּטֶּה' means 'the rod has budded/put forth' (צָץ = to blossom/bud), not 'the staff has flown away'. The Chinese '杖已飛逝' incorrectly renders 'צָץ' (budded/blossomed) as '飛逝' (flew away), changing the meaning. Also 'פָּרַח הַזָּדוֹן' means 'arrogance has blossomed' (פָּרַח = to blossom/flourish), which the Chinese renders as '驕傲已綻放' (arrogance has blossomed) — that is correct. The main error is the mistranslation of 'צָץ הַמַּטֶּה' as '杖已飛逝' instead of 'the rod has budded'.
